newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1997 H1 rice exports drop 25 percent on year.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1997 H1 rice exports drop 25 percent on year.

text.p: Thailand said on Friday its rice exports from January to early June dropped by more than 25 percent from the same period last year due to weaker global demand and lower-than-expected supplies in the country.
A senior commerce ministry official told Reuters that despite the slowdown, Thai rice prices remained high, especially those for glutinous rice and fragrant rice, because of strong demand.
The official said global demand for rice imports this year was projected to fall to 17.4 million tonnes from 19.3 million tonnes last year.
"Indonesia, for example, used to import one-two million tonnes a year but purchased only 600,000-700,000 tonnes this year. China buys less as local output increased, so does Bangladesh," he said.
"This year we might be able to export only 4.8-5.0 million tonnes from 5.3-5.5 million tonnes projected earlier," he said.
The commerce ministry last month revised the 1997 projection for rice exports down to around 5.0 million tonnes.
Thailand is still competitive on high quality rice such as the 100 percent grade and fragrant rice but is losing market share for lower grades to lower-cost producers in the region.
The official said demand for Thai fragrant and glutinous rice this year was high but supplies were limited.

"The second crop output was not much as we earlier anticipated," he said. The agriculture ministry estimated that 1996/97 rice output (April-March) was 21.27 million tonnes, of which 17.75 million came from the first crop.
"This year Laos bought 100,000 tonnes of glutinous rice from Thailand to offset shortfalls in the country, sending prices up," he said.

The paddy price of fragrant rice rose to an average of 7,775 baht ($311) per tonne this year from 5,320 baht last year. The glutinous rice paddy price edged up to 6,650 baht per tonne from 5,036 baht last year.
